reference_items.stem:
Class A and B each have 40 students.

[Image: Pie chart for Class A and bar graph for Class B]

There are more girls in Class A than in Class B. How many more?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two graphs representing student populations in Class A and Class B:
- On the left, a pie chart titled "Class A" showing a circle divided into two sectors. An unshaded sector representing one quarter of the circle (from 9 o'clock to 12 o'clock) is labeled "Boys". The remaining three-quarters of the circle is shaded grey and labeled "Girls".
- On the right, a bar graph titled "Class B" with a vertical axis labeled with values from 0 to 24 in increments of 4 (0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24) with horizontal grid lines. The horizontal axis has two categories: "Boys", with a light-grey bar of height 24, and "Girls", with a dark bar of height 16.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: a stack of square boxes in the corner of a room.]

Ann stacks these boxes in the corner of the room. All the boxes are the same size.
How many boxes does she use?
reference_items.figure_description:
An isometric drawing shows a stack of identical cube-shaped boxes resting in the corner of a room. Three line segments represent the room's edges meeting at the corner behind the stack: a vertical line extends straight up from the top-back corner of the stack, a line extends down and to the left from the bottom-left of the stack along the floor, and a line extends to the right from the bottom-right of the stack along the floor.

The stack rests on the floor against both walls. The base layer is completely filled, measuring 3 cubes deep along the left wall and 4 cubes wide along the back wall (a 3 by 4 grid of cubes).

A second layer of cubes is stacked on top against the corner in a stepped pattern:
- Along the back wall (row 1, closest to the back wall), the first 3 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the 4th column is 1 cube high.
- In the middle row (row 2), the first 2 columns from the left are 2 cubes high, and the remaining 2 columns are 1 cube high.
- In the front row (row 3), the first column on the left is 2 cubes high, and the remaining 3 columns are 1 cube high.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2007 and 2011 fourth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
